messages.text: I’ve recorded hashes for all 22 expected files in the affected golden families. They’ll stay unchanged through validation. The initial build has reached RQL and should finish before I apply the registry fix.

I’ll leave `failure_handler_state.rs` as you merged it. The fix belongs at the shared reason source: Go and Rust both emit `HandlerIdentityProof::Open`, so one registered content label covers both without changing row construction or the fail-closed treatment of unknown labels.

The audit found one more necessary part of the fix: identity proof can also stop on bounded resolution, cancellation or provider failures. I’ll preserve those execution-dependent marks in the Go/Rust producers while registering the source-backed identity gap as content. Verdicts and public labels will stay unchanged.

The producer audit is complete. Go’s incomplete resolution and limited reads need explicit execution marks. Rust already has a completion-aware proof wrapper I can reuse, preserving its result while marking unfinished attempts. Both changes stay local to failure-handler classification.

The extended test is still building, with no errors reported. This master contains fewer selected Go library tests than the previous head: the initial run passed 282, and I’ve recorded the exact removals and moved test.

The extended test has reached the final crates in its build. After it finishes, I’ll apply the operational-stop marks and run the complete validation set on the final source. The confirmed v53/v52 domains and policy token will remain unchanged.
The test build is still finishing MCP. The final source will distinguish reusable content uncertainty from operational stops, without changing the public `Open` identity or the handler-row shape.

I’ll also run the existing content-diagnostic admission tests. They cover budget refusal and cancelled memo fills, which are relevant checks now that the fix preserves operational marks separately from content gaps.

The extended reuse test passes for Scala, Go and Rust. The final producer changes are now applied as well: content gaps remain reusable, operational stops mark the read ledger, and proof results stay unchanged. I’m starting the full validation pass on this source.

The final-source library build is progressing without errors. Once it passes, the script will run the reason inventory, root suites, content-admission tests, token test, Clippy, fmt and drift. #7507 remains untouched.

The final library build is still running without errors. No further source edits are planned. Validation is running without `BIFROST_BLESS`, and I’ll check that the expected files match their recorded hashes.

The final library build has reached RQL without errors. The diff remains limited to the reason registry, its shared producer, operational marks in the Go/Rust hooks, and the incremental regression test.

All 282 selected Go/RQL library tests pass on the final source. The count is three lower than the previous head because master removed three tests and moved another to a different module; the full-name comparison is recorded. The reason-registry check is next.

The reason-inventory test is compiling. The completed final-source checks are still 282/282 Go/RQL tests; the earlier isolated reuse test also passed. The remaining checks will validate the final operational-mark changes and unchanged golden outputs.

The registry check is still building, with no errors reported. The repair preserves fail-closed handling for unknown labels; it registers only the existing identity label and keeps incomplete proof attempts execution-dependent.
The reason-registry test is still compiling its dependencies; no failure has appeared. I’m leaving the active build undisturbed and will continue through the remaining checks.

The registry build has reached the shared analysis crate, with no errors reported. After it finishes, the ordinary root run will include the empty-handler and RQL control goldens, plus the extended incremental failure-handler test.

The registry test is still compiling shared analysis; no failure has appeared. I’ll keep the validation running and report the actual test counts from this master, along with the test-name differences.

The reason-inventory test passes, including the content classification for the registered label and fail-closed handling for unknown labels. The ordinary root suites are now building with uv Python 3.12 and `python,devtools`.

The root build has reached the language-analysis crates without errors. The final receipt will include the actual test counts and verify that all five policy tokens occur once and the expected golden files remain unchanged.
The root build is still progressing without errors. The verification scripts and composition audit are saved; I’ll commit the fix after the remaining checks pass.
The root build has reached policy compilation, with no errors reported. The reason-inventory and Go/RQL library checks have passed; the root, admission, token and final lint checks remain.

I found one final operational edge in Go’s `recover` path: its capped builtin-shadow lookup can also return no answer. I’ll add the same execution mark there after the active root build finishes, then rerun the affected checks on the final source.

All 150 selected root tests pass, including the empty-handler and RQL control goldens and the extended reuse test. I’ve now added the final `recover` lookup mark and restarted validation. The registry check remains valid because its code and dependencies are unchanged by that last Go-only edit.
The final Go-only mark is compiling through Go analysis, tools and RQL. The preceding full root run passed 150/150; this pass will validate the final source before I commit it.
The final library pass is complete: 282/282 passed with the `recover` mark included. The root suites are running next, followed by admission, token, Clippy, fmt and drift.

The final root build has reached MCP without errors. I also checked the inner bounded Go lookups: incomplete limited reads propagate through the resolution session, so the outer execution mark covers them. No further source change is needed.
The root build is still running without errors. I’ll leave both worktrees stable while it finishes, then commit the fix if the remaining checks pass.

The final root run passes 150/150. All 10 content-diagnostic admission tests pass too, including budget refusal, cancelled memo fills, and the extended Scala/Go/Rust reuse test. The token check is next.

The token test is compiling its remaining dependencies. The final library, root and content-admission checks have passed, and all 22 expected files remain unchanged. Clippy, formatting and pack drift follow the token test.
The token-test build has reached the analysis crates without errors. Completed checks remain green; this test, Clippy, fmt and pack drift are the only checks left before the commit.

The token build has reached the policy crate without errors. The report draft is ready with the merge interaction, the test-count differences and the log paths; I’ll finalize it after the remaining checks pass.

The token test passes. Clippy is now running with `-D warnings` on the eight libraries. All requested tests and the additional content-admission checks have passed; fmt and pack drift are the last steps.
Clippy has reached the final library crates with no warnings reported. Formatting and pack drift remain; then I’ll commit the fix and report the head and receipts.

All checks pass, including Clippy, fmt and pack drift. I’m checking the final receipt and diff, then committing the five-file merge fix locally. The expected files, v53/v52 domains and policy tokens are unchanged.

Committed `7b73ea4cb5` fixing the diagnostic-admission interaction. All checks pass: 282 Go/RQL tests, 150 root tests, token tests, Clippy, fmt and drift. Master’s test changes explain the count differences.

No push; #7507 untouched. Detailed report and logs handed back.

I’ll inspect the grammar and binding walk, add the labeled-declaration regressions and statement audit, then validate and rerun the mux oracle. After committing, I’ll push with an explicit refspec, verify both remote heads, and leave the PR in draft.

The pinned Go grammar has no `statement` field on `labeled_statement`; it exposes the wrapped statement as an unnamed child. I’ll select that child through the grammar’s statement-supertype metadata, while accepting a `statement` field when present. This keeps nested-label unwrapping structural.

The baseline confirms that native navigation already resolves the new labeled bindings and their types correctly, while the shared static-type walk drops the inner guards. I’ve added single and nested labels, typed-error controls, and a labeled multi-name redeclaration case to check scope and visibility.

The audit found a separate pre-existing gap: the baseline CLI also drops an error guard inside a `for` body when the header declares the same name via `for_clause`. I’m recording the reproducer without changing that behavior here; fixing it would move answers beyond labeled shapes and need an identity decision.

The updated goldens pass. Labeled typed-error declarations now produce findings; identifier-initialized short declarations stay open under the unchanged positive classifier, instead of being dropped through the outer slice type. The appended navigation probes retain their baseline answers. I’m auditing every changed expected line now.

Understood. I’ll finish the validation already running and commit the labeled fix, then wait for the pushed #7507 head. After merging it, I’ll retain all prerequisite tokens and comments, set #7470 to v57/v56, and validate that merged head before the oracle run and push.

The labeled-only run has passed 282 library tests, 150 root tests, the reason inventory and all 10 admission tests. The audit found no moved expected lines outside the new labeled cases. I’m finishing token, lint and formatting checks before committing, then I’ll wait for your pushed prerequisite head.

Clippy passed on all eight libraries. Formatting is still running, with pack drift next. The audit accounts for every changed golden line, and the separate baseline `for_clause` issue remains outside this patch.

The labeled-only validation is complete: 282 libs, 150 root tests, reason inventory, admission tests, token test, Clippy, fmt and drift all pass. I’m committing the fix now, then waiting for your pushed #7507 head before merging and producing final evidence.

Committed the labeled fix as `2b0663d974`. The isolated checks pass and the statement and golden audits are complete. I’m waiting for the pushed #7507 head before merging, applying v57/v56, and running the final validation and oracle qualification.

Committed the labeled fix as `2b0663d974`; all isolated checks pass. Awaiting the pushed #7507 head before the required v57/v56 merge, final validation, oracle run and push.

Checkpoint report includes the statement audit and separate baseline `for_clause` gap.

I’ll audit and fix the statement-header bindings in the shared walk, then commit that separately from the label fix. I’ll leave the #7507 worktree untouched and wait for its pushed head before merging and running final validation.

The audit found the gap in `for`: its initializer sits inside a `for_clause`, which the walk skips when resolving a name in the loop body. `if` and both switch forms expose their initializer directly; select and range have existing binder handling. I’ll add controls for all six forms, including uses inside the statement and after it.

The fix now selects the `for_clause` initializer before applying visibility checks. The new controls cover all six header forms, including a loop condition and post expression, both `if` arms, switch cases, select, range, and uses after each statement. All three Go fixture files pass `go test` and `go vet`.

The header audit is complete. Only the `for_clause` initializer needs a code change; the existing paths cover the other five forms. The golden runners are rebuilding now. After auditing their output, I’ll commit this fix separately and wait for the pushed #7507 head before final validation.

The golden build is waiting for an existing mbx compilation of Go analysis. The source audit is done, and the fixture checks pass. I’ll let mbx finish, then inspect the golden changes; the full validation set will still run once after the prerequisite merge.

The pre-fix navigation probes resolve the new header cases correctly, including the loop condition and post expression and the uses after each statement. Select receive typing remains unresolved, as expected. This supports keeping the fix in the shared static-proof walk; no producer change is needed.

The audit will compare all 34 existing failure-handler rows and 27 existing navigation probes against the label-fix commit. The new controls also check that an initializer stays inside its statement and that a select case’s binding does not affect a sibling case.
Compilation has reached the policy crate with no errors reported so far. The source and fixture edits are finished; I’m waiting for the golden output before auditing and committing them.
No compile errors have appeared. The rebuild has reached runtime and MCP; the golden runners have not started yet. I haven’t changed identity values, merged a prerequisite, or pushed anything.

The rebuild is still running without errors. The expected behavior for the regression is an unknown handler row where the outer slice type previously caused a silent exclusion. The new cases retain the existing positive classification rules.

The build has reached the root binaries and test executables. Once the runners finish, I’ll audit their output and make the separate header-fix commit. The prerequisite merge remains pending the pushed #7507 head.

The build hit an mbx validation error: it discarded results because recorded build-script inputs changed during compilation. The tests have not run. I’ll let the remaining jobs finish, preserve the log, and retry the golden command.

The same mbx rejection affected the test executables, so no golden assertions ran. The root build script watches Git metadata, including the index and shared refs. I’ll avoid optional Git index writes during the retry and keep the failed-build evidence.

The retry is using the compiled dependencies and rebuilding the root artifacts. No build-script rejection has appeared so far. I’ll keep Git metadata untouched until it finishes, then audit the golden output and commit.

The retry is still compiling root artifacts without new errors. I haven’t started the full validation set, changed the allocated identity values, or touched the prerequisite worktree. Those steps remain pending the merged stack.

Only the large `suite_bench_policy` executable is still compiling; the other root artifacts have finished without another mbx rejection. After the runners finish, the audit will check all prior rows and probes and list the new cases separately.
The retry built successfully. The navigation and RQL golden runners have passed; the empty-handler runner is still running. Next I’ll audit the output and commit the header fix.

All three golden runners passed. The audit found one changed answer on the same source: the loop-body guard at `branches.go:273` now produces an unknown row instead of being silently excluded. All 34 prior rows and 27 prior navigation probes are unchanged, and the 53 navigation answers match the pre-fix binary. No golden answers moved outside the new cases.

Committed the header fix separately as `c974a7456c`, with the requested trailer. The audit found no answer changes outside the new cases. I’m now waiting for the pushed #7507 head; after merging it, I’ll set v57/v56, run final validation and the mux oracle, then push and verify without marking ready.

Committed separately as `c974a7456c`. Three golden runners passed; no answers changed outside the new cases.

Waiting for the pushed #7507 head before merging, final validation, mux qualification, and push verification. Nothing pushed.
